It's very weird-unlike S. flava var. rubricporporas, when the trap first opens on this prince george Co, VA plant, the color is pretty much determined at that point. posts.body_html:
Hi Guys:

Just joined ANOTHER forum - this one - but should be here. Guys, you need to start verifying provenance on your plants and ensure that these genotypes haven't been contaminated over time in culture. I can tell you this plant is NOT from Prince George County, VA. We've got the original germplasm from this now extirpated colony and they do NOT look like this.

Sincerely,

Phil Sheridan, Ph.D.
Director
Meadowview Biological
Research Station

posts.body_html:
Hi Phil,


yes, this was from Meadowview via mail order. While ordering, I remember asking if this was a slow growing plant, and you explained that it grows just as fast as a regular flava.

Can't recall the date, but I do remember receiving the package in the early summer. The rhizome was large, and the roots were not only healthy, but carefully packaged so there was no damage to them. One thing I clearly remember is that all the pitchers were chopped off to the base of the rhizome. There was a letter in the package stating that all of the traps were cut off due to California's agricultural restrictions.


This clone is very distinct, and at the time, there was no other plant in the collection that looked like it.

Not sure if this is the exact same clone, but here's some photographed at Meadowview that look very similar:



The clone I have can do this very same thing where the body turns almost solid red:
www.flickr.com/photos/60270758@N02/5834658358/


Not sure if this is the same plant?:
www.flickr.com/photos/60270758@N02/6039953925/

and the lid looks very similar to my clone:
www.flickr.com/photos/60270758@N02/5830421008/ Any idea what County and State these came from?

You're probably the most knowledgeable person on this planet when it comes to S. flavas in Virginia, so there's no doubt in my mind that a mistake was made in the ID. Perhaps it was thought that the virginia clone was sent out whereas instead, this wonderful plant was shipped out.

Hi Meizzwang:

I'm still puzzled by this since we have not sold Virginia S. flava by mail order, other than Pocahontas. There has to be some mistake here in communication. The plant you have is definitely not Prince George Virginia S. flava. The plant looks more like a gulf coast ornata - that we do sell.

If you had the year you purchased the plant, and season, I can pull our records and check the sale.

Best,

Phil

Thanks,

Phil
